mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% in a month coincides with a temporary boost in risk appetite, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3 in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns fail to outperform a 5-day rolling mean by at least 0.5% in 70% of similar inflation surprise events (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS labor market strength accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE unemployment suggests stronger wage growth and reduced hiring costs, both of which are associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: In 20-day windows where PAYEMS up and UNRATE down, SPX 20d returns are negative on >50% of occasions (median negative return > -0.2%).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO manufacturing index below 50 signals supply-side softness, which typically precedes a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as market anticipates slower growth.
failure_condition: Over 3 consecutive months of INDPRO < 50, 60-day forward returns remain non-negative in >70% of similar episodes (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in HOUST retail sales followed by a subsequent rise above the prior month's low creates a 'rebound effect', which is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as market interprets the recovery as demand stabilization.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls then rebounds in the same month
failure_condition: In 20 such rebound months, 5-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline (mean difference < 0.1%, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25 percentage points in a month, the discount rate for future cash flows is expected to increase, but if this coincides with strong macro demand (e.g., GDPC1 up), the adverse effect on equity valuations is muted, producing a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases >0.25pp and GDPC1 increases in the same month
regime_hint: federal funds hike during rising demand
failure_condition: In 50 such events, 20d forward returns are negative in >50% of cases (median < -0.2%).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-time drop in UNRATE below 4.5% in a month signals a sudden labor market slackening, which tends to precede a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days as investors anticipate slower growth.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.5 in the current month
regime_hint: unemployment rate surprise to the downside
failure_condition: Over 10 such episodes, 60-day forward returns are not significantly worse than a 5-day moving average (mean difference < -0.1%, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of RSAFS falling below 450 billion USD in monthly terms indicate persistent supply-side weakness, which predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days unless offset by a simultaneous sharp drop in inflation (CPIAUCSL > 0.4%).
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 450 for two consecutive months and CPIAUCSL > 0.4 in the current month
regime_hint: persistent supply weakness with inflation stickiness
failure_condition: In 30 such events, 20d forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline (median > -0.05%, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising for 3 consecutive months), S&P 500 forward returns turn negative over the next 60 days unless accompanied by a strong GDP demand signal (GDPC1 up >10% YoY).
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for 3 consecutive months and GDPC1 does not rise >10% YoY in the same period
regime_hint: prolonged monetary tightening without strong demand
failure_condition: In 20 such episodes, 60-day forward returns are not meaningfully worse than a 20-day moving average (median difference < -0.1%, p > 0.05).
